prices.title: Electricity prices
prices.description:
{status}

Set the **Buy price** and the **Sell price** — each is an energy price (market or fixed) plus markup and grid fee, with VAT or tax on top. **Price source and sensor** is needed while either price follows the market. Price level is optional. **← Back** keeps everything you confirmed.

menu_options.prices_remove: ✕ Remove electricity prices from this installation

price_feed.title: Price source and sensor
price_feed.description: Where the market price comes from, and the currency prices are shown in. {detected} A price sensor is only needed while the buy or sell price follows the market — with both prices fixed, choose **Other** and leave it blank.

data.currency: Display currency code (e.g. EUR, SEK, NOK, DKK, GBP)

data_description.price_sensor: Sensors from Nord Pool, ENTSO-e, Octopus Agile or Amber whose attributes hold today's and tomorrow's prices. Nord Pool is verified on a live install; the others follow each integration's documented format but are untested. **Other** lets you pick the source and sensor yourself.
data_description.price_export_sensor: Separate live export-price feeds found on this system (Octopus export rates, Amber feed-in). The one from the price sensor's integration is pre-selected; a market-based sell price then uses it instead of the import price. **None** keeps the sell price on the price sensor.
data_description.price_source: Nord Pool is verified on a live install. ENTSO-e, Octopus and Amber follow each integration's documented format but are untested.
data_description.nordpool_entity: The sensor from your price integration (Nord Pool, ENTSO-e, Octopus Agile or Amber) whose attributes hold today's and tomorrow's prices — for Octopus, the `…_current_day_rates` event entity. Leave blank when both prices are fixed.
data_description.price_export_entity: Only for a separate live export price (Octopus Outgoing — its `…_export_current_day_rates` event entity — or Amber feed-in). A market-based sell price then uses it instead of the import price. Leave blank otherwise.
data_description.nordpool_resolution: 15-minute is recommended where the market publishes it. With both prices fixed it sets the slot length.
data_description.currency: Only changes labels — prices stay per kWh in the price source's unit.
data_description.go_to: Confirm saves this page and returns to the menu (with **Other**, it opens the page for the source and sensor first); the ✕ option leaves it unchanged.

price_feed_manual.title: Price source and sensor: other
price_feed_manual.description: Pick the price integration and its sensor yourself.

data_description.nordpool_entity: The sensor from your price integration whose attributes hold today's and tomorrow's prices — for Octopus, the `…_current_day_rates` event entity. Leave blank when both prices are fixed.

price_buy.title: Buy price
price_buy.description:
{status}

What you pay per kWh: **(energy + markup + grid fee) × (1 + VAT)**. Start with **Price formula**. With 2 or 4 grid-fee tariffs, each schedule below says which tariff applies when.

price_buy_formula.title: Price formula — buy price
price_buy_formula.description: Buy price = **(energy + markup + grid fee) × (1 + VAT)**. The energy is the market price from the price source, or a fixed price. The grid fee can have 1, 2 or 4 tariffs; with more than one, set their fees and schedules in the Buy price menu.

data.holidays: Public holidays have their own schedule
data.seasons: Summer and winter have their own schedules

data_description.energy: The market price follows the price source slot by slot; a fixed price is entered below.

data_description.vat: Applied to the sum of energy, markup and grid fee.

data_description.weekends: Only with 2 or 4 tariffs. Off: Saturdays and Sundays follow the workday schedule.
data_description.holidays: Only with 2 or 4 tariffs. The national public holidays of the country set in Home Assistant; they take precedence over weekends.
data_description.seasons: Only with 2 or 4 tariffs. Every day type then gets a summer and a winter schedule.
data_description.summer_start: Only with seasons. The first day of the summer schedule.

price_levels.title: Price level
price_levels.description:
sunSale publishes whether the current price is cheap, normal or expensive — as the "Price level" sensor and the "Cheap price" / "Expensive price" binary sensors — so your automations and other integrations can react, e.g. heat extra hot water while it is cheap, or put heating and air conditioning in energy-saving mode while it is expensive. sunSale itself does not control anything with it.

Each slot's buy price (with fees and tax) is ranked within its day.

data.price_level_cheap_share: Cheapest part of the day counted as cheap (%)
data.price_level_expensive_share: Dearest part of the day counted as expensive (%)
data.price_level_cheap_below: Always cheap at or below (per kWh, optional)
data.price_level_expensive_above: Always expensive at or above (per kWh, optional)

data_description.price_level_cheap_share: 25 % means the cheapest 6 hours of each day are "cheap".
data_description.price_level_expensive_share: 25 % means the dearest 6 hours of each day are "expensive". The rest is "normal".
data_description.price_level_cheap_below: Overrides the ranking — any buy price at or below this is cheap, even on an expensive day. Leave blank to rank only.
data_description.price_level_expensive_above: Overrides the ranking — any buy price at or above this is expensive, even on a cheap day. Leave blank to rank only.
data_description.go_to: Confirm saves this page and returns to the menu; the ✕ option leaves it unchanged.

price_forecast.title: Price forecast weather (optional)
price_forecast.description:
{detected}

The week-ahead price forecast predicts each unsettled day from this install's own price history, corrected by weather only as far as that correction has measurably helped. This page says which weather entity it reads.

data_description.weather_entity: Its **daily** forecast is used (wind, temperature and, where published, cloud cover), so the horizon is whatever your weather integration publishes — six days for met.no. Days beyond it fall back to history alone.

bms.title: Dedicated battery BMS (optional)
bms.description:
A pack-level BMS usually reports state of charge more accurately and more often than the inverter does. Pick the battery device and sunSale finds its sensors on the next page; its readings are then preferred, falling back to the inverter for anything the BMS does not publish.

Leave this empty to read the battery from the inverter alone.

data_description.bms_device: Only devices publishing a state of charge are listed. Confirming with this empty removes a BMS set earlier.
data_description.go_to: Confirm opens the device's sensors for you to check; the ✕ option leaves this page unchanged.

bms_details.title: Battery BMS sensors
bms_details.description: These are the sensors found on **{device}**. Check them and correct any that look wrong.

data_description.bms_battery_soc: Required for the BMS to be used at all: sunSale will not plan against a state of charge it cannot read, so without this one the inverter stays the battery source.
data_description.bms_battery_power: Signed, positive while charging. A BMS that reports discharge as positive needs a template sensor that flips the sign. Left unset, pack power comes from the inverter.
data_description.go_to: Confirm saves this page and returns to the menu; the ✕ option leaves it unchanged.

sources.title: Inverter power sensors (optional)
sources.description:
{detected}

Every sensor here is optional and each one only sharpens a chart or a correction — sunSale falls back to its own estimate for anything left unset.

data.inverter_entity_ac_port_power: AC grid-port power (signed, positive = inverter → grid)

data_description.inverter_entity_pv_power: Feeds the observed generation series and the clear-sky calibration.
data_description.inverter_entity_ac_port_power: Needed together with the backup port for the observed consumption and losses series: both are part of the power balance, so leaving either out switches those two series off.
data_description.inverter_entity_backup_power: Reads ~0 unless the inverter is bridging backup-protected loads with the grid down. Also part of the consumption / losses balance.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_import_power: Only for inverters that publish each direction separately. Left blank, sunSale splits the signed net grid sensor itself, which is what most installs do.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_export_power: The export half of the pair above; set both or neither.
data_description.go_to: Confirm saves this page and returns to the menu; the ✕ option leaves it unchanged.

sources_energy.title: Energy counters (optional)
sources_energy.description:
{detected}

Running totals, all optional. Today's counters correct each day's series as it is measured; yesterday's are the best source for finalising the day just gone.

data_description.inverter_entity_solar_energy: Daily-resetting counter used to correct the generation series at the end of each day.
data_description.inverter_entity_household_consumption_en: Daily-resetting counter. Blank is fine — baseload is worked out from the other readings.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_import_energy: Daily-resetting counter; the authoritative total the grid series is corrected against.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_export_energy: Daily-resetting counter; the export half of the pair above.
data_description.inverter_entity_battery_charge_energy: Daily-resetting counter feeding the battery-capacity estimate. Without it the estimate stays at the nominal capacity you entered instead of learning the real one.
data_description.inverter_entity_battery_discharge_energy: The discharge half of the pair above; the estimate needs both.
data_description.inverter_entity_generation_yesterday: A counter your inverter has already finalised for yesterday. This is the best source for the end-of-day correction — unlike a reading taken just before midnight it cannot be thrown off by clock drift or by when the counter resets.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_import_yesterday: Yesterday's finalised import total, used the same way.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_export_yesterday: Yesterday's finalised export total, used the same way.
data_description.go_to: Confirm saves this page and returns to the menu; the ✕ option leaves it unchanged.

forecast.title: Solar forecast
forecast.description:
{detected}

Pick every solar forecast that covers this property — one per array (roof side, carport, …), as many as you have; they are added together.

data_description.solar_forecast_device_ids: Each one's "energy production today" sensor is found automatically. What each resolved to is listed above, so a device that exposes nothing recognisable is visible rather than silent.
data_description.detected_sensors: Forecast sensors on this system that none of the integrations above already covers — an integration sunSale does not recognise, or a sensor built by hand. Recognised by the per-slot forecast data they publish, so anything listed here is readable.
data_description.solar_forecast_entities: For an array whose sensor is in neither list. Use its "today" sensor: the other days are found by substituting the word, so a "tomorrow" or "d3" sensor will not work. The three fields are added together and de-duplicated, so an array can never count twice.
data_description.go_to: Confirm saves this page and returns to the menu; the ✕ option leaves it unchanged.

error.price_entity_required: {source} is a live price source, so it needs the price sensor from that integration. Pick it here, or make both the buy and the sell price fixed if you have no live price feed.
error.export_feed_mismatch: The export-price feed must come from the same price integration as the price sensor — sunSale reads it only there. Pick the matching feed, or None.
error.invalid_band_time: Start time must be 24-hour HH:MM between 00:00 and 23:59, e.g. 06:30.
error.duplicate_band_start: Another band already starts at this time — every band needs its own start time.
error.invalid_currency: Currency must be a 3-letter ISO code such as EUR, GBP, SEK or AUD.
error.invalid_capacity: Nominal capacity must be greater than 0 kWh.
error.invalid_price: Battery purchase price must be greater than 0 — it sets the wear cost of every cycle.
error.invalid_cycle_life: Rated cycle life must be greater than 0 (typical LFP: 6000).
error.invalid_charge_power: Max charge power must be greater than 0 kW.
error.invalid_discharge_power: Max discharge power must be greater than 0 kW.
error.invalid_voltage: Nominal DC bus voltage must be greater than 0 V (e.g. 51.2 for a low-voltage LFP pack).
error.invalid_min_soc: Minimum SoC is a percentage from 0 up to, but not including, 100.
error.invalid_max_soc: Maximum SoC is a percentage above 0, up to 100.
error.soc_range_inverted: Maximum SoC must be higher than Minimum SoC.
error.invalid_efficiency: Round-trip efficiency is a percentage above 0, up to 100 (typical: 85–95).
error.platform_not_implemented: {platform} isn't supported yet. Selectable: Solis, Huawei, SolaX, Sungrow, GoodWe, Deye, and "No inverter — metering only".
error.invalid_inverter_power: Inverter rated AC power must be greater than 0 kW.
error.invalid_export_limit: Max export power cannot be negative — enter 0 for a zero-export site.
error.level_shares_overlap: Cheap and expensive together cannot be more than 100 % of the day — a slot can't be both.
error.level_limits_inverted: "Always expensive at or above" must be higher than "Always cheap at or below".
error.invalid_season_date: Enter a calendar day as MM-DD, e.g. 04-01.
error.seasons_same_start: Summer and winter cannot start on the same day.
error.schedule_empty: Fill in at least one row — e.g. 00:00 with T1 for one tariff all day.
error.bms_no_soc: That device publishes no state of charge, so sunSale could not read the battery from it. Pick the device that reports the pack's state of charge, or leave the field empty to read the battery from the inverter.

price_sell_formula.description: Sell price = **(energy − deduction − grid fee) × (1 − tax)**. The energy is the market price from the price source — or the separate live export price where the source has one — or a fixed feed-in price. The grid fee can have 1, 2 or 4 tariffs; with more than one, set their fees and schedules in the Sell price menu.

data.fixed_price: Fixed sell price, e.g. a feed-in tariff (per kWh)
data.holidays: Public holidays have their own schedule
data.seasons: Summer and winter have their own schedules

data_description.vat: Deducted from what is left after the deduction and grid fee. 0 when you are not taxed on it.
data_description.tariffs: 1 = the same grid fee at all times. 2 or 4 = the fee depends on the time of day.
data_description.weekends: Only with 2 or 4 tariffs. Off: Saturdays and Sundays follow the workday schedule.
data_description.holidays: Only with 2 or 4 tariffs. The national public holidays of the country set in Home Assistant; they take precedence over weekends.
data_description.seasons: Only with 2 or 4 tariffs. Every day type then gets a summer and a winter schedule.

Which grid-fee tariff applies when. Each row switches to its tariff at its time (local, 24 h); the tariff runs until the next row's time, wrapping past midnight — a single row at 00:00 means one tariff all day. Leave unused rows blank.

Tariffs: {fees}

price_levels.title: Price level
price_levels.description:
sunSale publishes whether the current price is cheap, normal or expensive — as the "Price level" sensor and the "Cheap price" / "Expensive price" binary sensors — so your automations and other integrations can react, e.g. heat extra hot water while it is cheap, or put heating and air conditioning in energy-saving mode while it is expensive. sunSale itself does not control anything with it.

Each slot's buy price (with fees and tax) is ranked within its day.

data.price_level_cheap_share: Cheapest part of the day counted as cheap (%)
data.price_level_expensive_share: Dearest part of the day counted as expensive (%)
data.price_level_cheap_below: Always cheap at or below (per kWh, optional)
data.price_level_expensive_above: Always expensive at or above (per kWh, optional)

data_description.price_level_cheap_share: 25 % means the cheapest 6 hours of each day are "cheap".
data_description.price_level_expensive_share: 25 % means the dearest 6 hours of each day are "expensive". The rest is "normal".
data_description.price_level_cheap_below: Overrides the ranking — any buy price at or below this is cheap, even on an expensive day. Leave blank to rank only.
data_description.price_level_expensive_above: Overrides the ranking — any buy price at or above this is expensive, even on a cheap day. Leave blank to rank only.

bms.title: Dedicated battery BMS (optional)
bms.description:
A pack-level BMS usually reports state of charge more accurately and more often than the inverter does. Pick the battery device and sunSale finds its sensors on the next page; its readings are then preferred, falling back to the inverter for anything the BMS does not publish.

Leave this empty to read the battery from the inverter alone.

data_description.bms_device: Only devices publishing a state of charge are listed. Confirming with this empty removes a BMS set earlier.
data_description.go_to: Confirm opens the device's sensors for you to check; the ✕ option leaves this page unchanged.

bms_details.description: These are the sensors found on **{device}**. Check them and correct any that look wrong.

data_description.bms_battery_soc: Required for the BMS to be used at all: sunSale will not plan against a state of charge it cannot read, so without this one the inverter stays the battery source.
data_description.bms_battery_power: Signed, positive while charging. A BMS that reports discharge as positive needs a template sensor that flips the sign. Left unset, pack power comes from the inverter.

sources.title: Inverter power sensors (optional)
sources.description:
{detected}

Every sensor here is optional and each one only sharpens a chart or a correction — sunSale falls back to its own estimate for anything left unset.

data.inverter_entity_ac_port_power: AC grid-port power (signed, positive = inverter → grid)

data_description.inverter_entity_pv_power: Feeds the observed generation series and the clear-sky calibration.
data_description.inverter_entity_ac_port_power: Needed together with the backup port for the observed consumption and losses series: both are part of the power balance, so leaving either out switches those two series off.
data_description.inverter_entity_backup_power: Reads ~0 unless the inverter is bridging backup-protected loads with the grid down. Also part of the consumption / losses balance.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_import_power: Only for inverters that publish each direction separately. Left blank, sunSale splits the signed net grid sensor itself, which is what most installs do.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_export_power: The export half of the pair above; set both or neither.

sources_energy.title: Energy counters (optional)
sources_energy.description:
{detected}

Running totals, all optional. Today's counters correct each day's series as it is measured; yesterday's are the best source for finalising the day just gone.

data_description.inverter_entity_solar_energy: Daily-resetting counter used to correct the generation series at the end of each day.
data_description.inverter_entity_household_consumption_en: Daily-resetting counter. Blank is fine — baseload is worked out from the other readings.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_import_energy: Daily-resetting counter; the authoritative total the grid series is corrected against.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_export_energy: Daily-resetting counter; the export half of the pair above.
data_description.inverter_entity_battery_charge_energy: Daily-resetting counter feeding the battery-capacity estimate. Without it the estimate stays at the nominal capacity you entered instead of learning the real one.
data_description.inverter_entity_battery_discharge_energy: The discharge half of the pair above; the estimate needs both.
data_description.inverter_entity_generation_yesterday: A counter your inverter has already finalised for yesterday. This is the best source for the end-of-day correction — unlike a reading taken just before midnight it cannot be thrown off by clock drift or by when the counter resets.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_import_yesterday: Yesterday's finalised import total, used the same way.
data_description.inverter_entity_grid_export_yesterday: Yesterday's finalised export total, used the same way.

forecast.title: Solar forecast
forecast.description:
{detected}

Pick every solar forecast that covers this property — one per array (roof side, carport, …), as many as you have; they are added together.

data_description.solar_forecast_device_ids: Each one's "energy production today" sensor is found automatically. What each resolved to is listed above, so a device that exposes nothing recognisable is visible rather than silent.
data_description.detected_sensors: Forecast sensors on this system that none of the integrations above already covers — an integration sunSale does not recognise, or a sensor built by hand. Recognised by the per-slot forecast data they publish, so anything listed here is readable.
data_description.solar_forecast_entities: For an array whose sensor is in neither list. Use its "today" sensor: the other days are found by substituting the word, so a "tomorrow" or "d3" sensor will not work. The three fields are added together and de-duplicated, so an array can never count twice.

error.price_entity_required: {source} is a live price source, so it needs the price sensor from that integration. Pick it here, or make both the buy and the sell price fixed if you have no live price feed.
error.export_feed_mismatch: The export-price feed must come from the same price integration as the price sensor — sunSale reads it only there. Pick the matching feed, or None.
error.invalid_band_time: Start time must be 24-hour HH:MM between 00:00 and 23:59, e.g. 06:30.
error.duplicate_band_start: Another band already starts at this time — every band needs its own start time.
error.invalid_currency: Currency must be a 3-letter ISO code such as EUR, GBP, SEK or AUD.
error.invalid_capacity: Nominal capacity must be greater than 0 kWh.
error.invalid_price: Battery purchase price must be greater than 0 — it sets the wear cost of every cycle.
error.invalid_cycle_life: Rated cycle life must be greater than 0 (typical LFP: 6000).
error.invalid_charge_power: Max charge power must be greater than 0 kW.
error.invalid_discharge_power: Max discharge power must be greater than 0 kW.
error.invalid_voltage: Nominal DC bus voltage must be greater than 0 V (e.g. 51.2 for a low-voltage LFP pack).
error.invalid_min_soc: Minimum SoC is a percentage from 0 up to, but not including, 100.
error.invalid_max_soc: Maximum SoC is a percentage above 0, up to 100.
error.soc_range_inverted: Maximum SoC must be higher than Minimum SoC.
error.invalid_efficiency: Round-trip efficiency is a percentage above 0, up to 100 (typical: 85–95).
error.platform_not_implemented: {platform} isn't supported yet. Selectable: Solis, Huawei, SolaX, Sungrow, GoodWe, Deye, and "No inverter — metering only".
error.invalid_inverter_power: Inverter rated AC power must be greater than 0 kW.
error.invalid_export_limit: Max export power cannot be negative — enter 0 for a zero-export site.
error.level_shares_overlap: Cheap and expensive together cannot be more than 100 % of the day — a slot can't be both.
error.level_limits_inverted: "Always expensive at or above" must be higher than "Always cheap at or below".
error.invalid_season_date: Enter a calendar day as MM-DD, e.g. 04-01.
error.seasons_same_start: Summer and winter cannot start on the same day.
error.schedule_empty: Fill in at least one row — e.g. 00:00 with T1 for one tariff all day.
error.bms_no_soc: That device publishes no state of charge, so sunSale could not read the battery from it. Pick the device that reports the pack's state of charge, or leave the field empty to read the battery from the inverter.

price_feed_dead.title: sunSale has no electricity prices
price_feed_dead.description:
The price sensor `{entity_id}` has been unavailable for a while, and reloading the integration that provides it {reloads} times did not bring it back.

Without market prices sunSale cannot plan: it will not charge, discharge or sell on price, and the inverter is left in its fallback mode.

Some price integrations fetch once when the sensor is created and never retry, so a brief network or upstream API failure at Home Assistant startup disables them permanently. Check that integration, then restart Home Assistant. This message clears itself as soon as the sensor reports a price again.
